record.title: SpecOpt reports residue-aware optimization of predicted molecular selectivity
record.summary: The preprint proposes optimizing ligand specificity by contrasting predicted residue contacts for a target and up to three off-target proteins. On a 915-compound ChEMBL-derived benchmark, the authors report that 776 compounds (84.8%) improved the target-minus-off-target AutoDock Vina score gap, with the mean changing from −0.718 to +0.472 kcal/mol and mean Tanimoto similarity of 0.72 to the starting molecules. The reported results are docking scores, not measured binding or experimental selectivity.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On a 915-compound ChEMBL-derived benchmark, the authors report an improved target-minus-off-target Vina-score gap for 776 compounds (84.8%); the mean changes from −0.718 to +0.472 kcal/mol, with mean Tanimoto similarity 0.72.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a residue-identity ablation, the paper reports no improvement for 29 of 29 compounds; in a five-off-target check, all five tested off-target scores weakened for 5 of 20 compounds.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent execution or reproduction of the docking benchmark was conducted; the linked anonymous code page did not expose usable source in this review.
Predicted docking-score gaps have not been validated against measured binding affinity or experimental selectivity.

brief.importance_rationale: If validated, optimizing predicted target selectivity while constraining similarity could change local choices in computational hit prioritization. The consequence is meaningful for specialist molecular-design workflows, but the measured evidence is limited to docking and selected off-targets.
limitations: Results rely on AutoDock Vina docking scores and do not establish experimental binding affinity, selectivity or biological activity.
The main benchmark considers up to three off-targets; the five-off-target check covers only 20 compounds and weakens all five tested scores for 5 compounds.
The residue-identity ablation reports no improvement across 29 compounds, indicating sensitivity to residue representation.
The linked code was not publicly accessible in the reviewed source check; no implementation run or independent reproduction was conducted.

On a 915-compound ChEMBL-derived benchmark, the authors report that 776 compounds (84.8%) improved the target-minus-off-target AutoDock Vina score gap, with the mean changing from −0.718 to +0.472 kcal/mol and mean Tanimoto similarity of 0.72 to the starting molecules. technical.claimed_result: The authors report improved target-minus-off-target AutoDock Vina score gaps for 776/915 compounds (84.8%), with mean gap changing from −0.718 to +0.472 kcal/mol and mean Tanimoto similarity 0.72. These are docking results.
technical.mechanism: Optimize ligand candidates using the difference between predicted target-residue and off-target-residue contacts, with a similarity constraint; the benchmark considers up to three off-target proteins.
technical.regime: Computational benchmark derived from 915 ChEMBL compounds, target plus up to three off-targets, predicted residue contacts and AutoDock Vina scoring; a limited five-off-target robustness check covers 20 compounds.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares optimized compounds with starting compounds under its own docking and contact-difference objective; no experimental affinity or selectivity measurement is reported.

brief.title: SpecOpt reports residue-aware optimization of predicted molecular selectivity
brief.why_it_matters: If validated experimentally, residue-aware optimization could help prioritize molecules that favor a target while limiting predicted binding to selected off-targets. The current evidence supports a computational screening method and benchmark result; it does not establish biochemical selectivity or therapeutic performance.
